knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite submodular minimization with explicit access and feasibility models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A submodular-minimization benchmark instance is a tuple \((V,f,\mathcal{F},\mathsf{Access})\), where \(V\) is finite, \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}\) is submodular, \(\varnothing
eq\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^V\), and \(\mathsf{Access}\) specifies either a value oracle or an explicit representation. The task is
\[\min\{f(S):S\in\mathcal{F}\}.\]
A submission reports \(S\), its recomputed value \(f(S)\), elapsed resources, and access counts. An optimality certificate must provide a verifiable lower bound \(L\) satisfying \(L=f(S)\); a reported value alone does not certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The benchmark minimizes a finite submodular function over a declared feasible family and records both computational resources and checkable optimality evidence.
knowledge_statements.title: Submodular-Minimization Benchmarks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The benchmark definition is coherent and appropriately distinguishes a reported value from an optimality certificate, but it lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator for the submodular-minimization and certification claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Submodular-Maximization Benchmarks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone nonnegative submodular maximization under an explicitly specified combinatorial constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constrained submodular-maximization benchmark is a tuple \((V,f,\mathcal{F},\mathsf{Access})\), where \(V\) is finite, \(f:2^V\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is monotone and submodular, \(\varnothing\neq\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^V\), and \(\mathsf{Access}\) declares the value-oracle or explicit-input model. The task is \[f^\star=\max\{f(S):S\in\mathcal{F}\}.\] A valid submission gives \(S\in\mathcal{F}\), its recomputed value, its access count, and its running time. If a certificate establishes \(f^\star\leq U\) with \(U>0\), then \(f(S)/U\leq f(S)/f^\star\), so \(f(S)/U\) is a certified lower bound on the achieved approximation ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The benchmark maximizes a monotone submodular value over a declared constraint family and validates feasibility, value, resource use, and any certified lower bound on the achieved approximation ratio.
assumptions_latex: The objective is nonnegative, monotone, and submodular on a finite ground set.
The feasible family is explicitly declared and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A submitted feasible set is scored by its value and, when a valid positive upper bound \(U\) is supplied, by the certified ratio lower bound \(f(S)/U\).

notation.meaning: certified upper bound on the optimum

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constrained submodular maximization is determined by its objective, feasible family, and access model

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Convex Exchange-Algorithm Benchmarks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Steepest unit-exchange descent for finite-domain \(M\)-convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an objective \(g:\mathbb{Z}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}g\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate every exchange \(x^k-e_i+e_j\in\operatorname{dom}g\). If \[g(x^k)\leq g(x^k-e_i+e_j)\quad\text{for every feasible pair }(i,j),\] stop and output \(x^k\). Otherwise choose a feasible pair minimizing \(g(x^k-e_i+e_j)\), set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-e_i+e_j\), and continue. The benchmark records iterations, evaluated exchanges, and objective evaluations. If \(g\) is \(M\)-convex, the stopping condition certifies global minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly take a best improving feasible unit exchange; for an M-convex objective, absence of an improving exchange certifies global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The effective domain \(\operatorname{dom}g\) is finite and nonempty.
The objective \(g\) is \(M\)-convex when the global-optimality conclusion is invoked.
Every exchange move and objective value can be evaluated exactly or using a declared comparison tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an exchange-locally minimal point; under the \(M\)-convex assumption, that point is globally minimal.

notation.meaning: extended-real objective on the integer lattice

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: steepest feasible unit exchange is a canonical local-search primitive for M-convex objectives

children.title: Oracle-Complexity Validation
children.top_down_role: Empirical assessment of oracle-use claims across benchmark families.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Complexity Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-based validation of deterministic value-oracle query counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a deterministic oracle algorithm with declared implementation and initial state, an oracle-complexity certificate consists of a transcript \(T=((S_1,y_1),\ldots,(S_q,y_q))\), a claimed budget \(B\), and an output \(x\). Validation checks \(y_i=\mathcal{O}_f(S_i)\) for every \(i\), replays the declared algorithm and confirms that its \(i\)-th query is \(S_i\), confirms that replay terminates with \(x\), and verifies \(q\leq B\). Repeated queries count repeatedly unless the benchmark explicitly declares a caching model. Computation performed between queries is reported separately and does not alter the oracle count \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A replayable query transcript validates oracle answers, deterministic algorithm behavior, final output, and compliance with the declared query budget.
assumptions_latex: The deterministic algorithm, implementation, initial state, and value oracle \(\mathcal{O}_f\) are declared.
Each oracle call, complete query, and response is logged before termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run validates the oracle-complexity claim exactly when transcript answers and deterministic replay are consistent, replay yields \(x\), and \(q\leq B\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic query complexity can be checked from a complete reproducible oracle transcript and explicit call count

children.title: Approximation-Guarantee Validation
children.top_down_role: Empirical assessment of approximation-quality claims across benchmark regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation-Guarantee Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent certificate for a maximization problem accessed through a value oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\), let \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^V\), and define \(\mathrm{OPT}=\max_{T\in\mathcal F}f(T)\). For \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), an independently verified tuple \((S,v,U)\) certifies an \((\alpha,\varepsilon)\)-guarantee when \(S\in\mathcal F\), \(|v-f(S)|\le\varepsilon_v\), \(U\ge\mathrm{OPT}\), and \(v-\varepsilon_v\ge\alpha U-\varepsilon\). Consequently, \(f(S)\ge\alpha\mathrm{OPT}-\varepsilon\). Every oracle response used to establish \(v\) or \(U\) must be reproducible from the recorded query transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible solution has the claimed approximation guarantee when independently checked value and optimum-bound certificates imply its objective is at least the stated fraction of optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f:2^V\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is accessed through a reproducible value oracle.
\(S\in\mathcal F\) and \(U\ge\mathrm{OPT}\) are independently verifiable.
\(\alpha\in[0,1]\) and \(\varepsilon,\varepsilon_v\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(S)\ge\alpha\mathrm{OPT}-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: certified upper bound on the maximization optimum
recorded value estimate for the returned set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf and the displayed implication is mathematically consistent, but no citation supports the oracle-transcript and tolerance protocol. The plain statement also omits the additive and value-estimation tolerances present in the LaTeX claim. An authoritative approximation-oracle source and a benchmark-protocol source are required.

children.title: Oracle-Budget Regimes
children.top_down_role: Benchmark settings organized by available oracle budget and oracle cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Budget Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget classes for reproducible value-oracle benchmarks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance with ground-set size \(n\), let \(q\) be the number of distinct oracle calls in the validated transcript and let \(B(n)\in\mathbb N\) be the announced budget. The run is budget-feasible exactly when \(q\le B(n)\). A benchmark regime is the sequence \((B(n))_{n\ge1}\); it is constant if \(B(n)=O(1)\), linear if \(B(n)=\Theta(n)\), polynomial if \(B(n)=n^{O(1)}\), and unrestricted when no finite cap is imposed. Repeated cached queries count once only if caching is declared before execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle-budget regime specifies how many distinct oracle calls are permitted as instance size grows, with an explicit convention for cached repeated queries.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle query and response is recorded in an auditable transcript.
The instance size is the ground-set cardinality \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\le B(n)\) is the budget-feasibility predicate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate content kind, but the budget taxonomy and cache-accounting convention are benchmark-specific and uncited. The named asymptotic classes overlap, so a source or explicit protocol must clarify whether they are merely properties or intended as mutually exclusive regimes.

children.title: Guarantee-Tightness Instances
children.top_down_role: Instances selected to expose tight, loose, or instance-sensitive approximation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Guarantee-Tightness Instances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic tightness relative to an algorithm and oracle-budget sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a maximization algorithm \(A\), approximation factor \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), and budgets \(B_k\). A sequence of instances \((I_k)_{k\ge1}\), with optima \(\mathrm{OPT}_k>0\), is guarantee-tight for \((A,\alpha)\) under those budgets if every validated run uses at most \(B_k\) oracle calls and its returned solution \(S_k\) satisfies \(f_k(S_k)/\mathrm{OPT}_k\to\alpha\). For a randomized algorithm, the ratio is replaced by \(\mathbb E[f_k(S_k)]/\mathrm{OPT}_k\), with the expectation taken over the algorithm's declared randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A benchmark family is tight when the validated performance ratio of the tested algorithm converges to its stated worst-case approximation factor.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathrm{OPT}_k>0\) for every instance.
Each run obeys its declared oracle budget \(B_k\).
Randomized runs declare the probability model used for expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k(S_k)/\mathrm{OPT}_k=\alpha\), or the corresponding expected-value equality.

notation.meaning: solution returned on the k-th instance
oracle budget for the k-th instance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the tightness-instance leaf, but no source supports this particular budget-conditioned definition. For randomized algorithms, the phrase "every validated run" does not align cleanly with the expected-value ratio and leaves the sampling or exact-expectation validation protocol unspecified.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Feasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validation for a mixed-integer linear primal candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasible set \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). A reported vector \(\hat x\) passes exact primal-feasibility validation if and only if \(A\hat x\le b\), \(C\hat x=d\), and \(\hat x_i\in\mathbb Z\) for all \(i\in I\). Under finite-precision validation with declared tolerances, each equality, inequality, and integrality test must instead use its separately specified tolerance; passing a relaxed test does not establish exact membership in \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is exactly primal feasible precisely when it satisfies every inequality, equality, and declared integrality restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,C,d\) and the integrality index set \(I\) are independently available.
Exact validation uses exact arithmetic or certified representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x\in P\).

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2 The Primal-Dual Algorithm p. 105

children.title: Dual Feasibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks focused on the validity of reported dual solutions or dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Feasibility Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for the dual of a standard minimization linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal program \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\), consider its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\). A reported dual vector \(\hat y\) passes exact dual-feasibility validation if and only if \(\hat y\ge0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\hat y\le c\). These predicates must be checked independently from the optimization routine; a finite-precision implementation must disclose its componentwise feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual candidate is feasible exactly when it is nonnegative and its transpose constraint residual satisfies every dual inequality.
assumptions_latex: The primal is in the displayed minimization form.
All data have exact or certified numerical representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat y\in\{y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\).
